Pure Byte-Level Specification of the Signal PQXDH Handshake and First Message

Trusted: the statement. Machine-free functional model of the PQXDH key agreement (Model.initiateKeys, Model.acceptKeys) and first-message key schedule (Model.initiate, Model.accept) of libsignal-protocol v0.105.4 over byte lists (Bytes := List UInt8), parameterized by Primitives, together with reference cryptographic constructions, the structural and algebraic well-formedness bundle WellFormedPrimitivesδ (without perfect KEM decapsulation correctness, DEV-PQ21), and functional correctness PqxdhCorrect. See Computational/docs/TRUSTED_BASE.md.

def buildSecretsL164–168 ↗#

Assembles the 160-byte (no OPK) or 192-byte (with OPK) secrets buffer (pqxdh.rs:202-231).

def buildSecrets (dh1 dh2 dh3 : Bytes) (dh4? : Option Bytes) (ss : Bytes) : Bytes := match dh4? with | none => F_X25519 ++ dh1 ++ dh2 ++ dh3 ++ ss | some dh4 => F_X25519 ++ dh1 ++ dh2 ++ dh3 ++ dh4 ++ ss

def pbVarintL170–178 ↗#

Protobuf base-128 varint (prost::encoding::encode_varint): 7 bits per byte, least significant group first, high bit set on every byte but the last.

def pbVarint (n : Nat) : Bytes := go n n where /-- Structural on the fuel `f` (so the kernel reduces it); `f = n` is always enough. -/ go : Nat → Nat → Bytes | 0, n => [n.toUInt8] | f + 1, n => if n < 128 then [n.toUInt8] else (n % 128 + 128).toUInt8 :: go f (n / 128)

def pbBytesFieldL180–182 ↗#

Protobuf bytes field tag (wire type 2): key byte 8·tag + 2, length varint, contents.

def pbBytesField (tag : Nat) (b : Bytes) : Bytes := (8 * tag + 2).toUInt8 :: (pbVarint b.length ++ b)

def firstMsgADL184–194 ↗#

First-message associated data authenticated by the 8-byte MAC in SignalMessage::compute_mac (protocol.rs:214-235): ser(ikA) ‖ ser(ikB), then the version byte 0x44 and the prost encoding of the inner SignalMessage header fields: ratchet_key = 1 (encodeEC ephAPk), counter = 2 and previous_counter = 3 (both 0 for the first message) and, if non-empty, pq_ratchet = 5. The first firstMsgHdrLen bytes are the fields that precede the ciphertext; aeadMacInput inserts the ciphertext field (ciphertext = 4) there, so the MAC input has prost's tag order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. addresses = 6 is omitted (DEV-PQ31).

def firstMsgAD (ikA ikB ephAPk pqRatchetMsg : Bytes) : Bytes := encodeEC ikA ++ encodeEC ikB ++ [0x44] ++ pbBytesField 1 (encodeEC ephAPk) ++ [0x10, 0x00, 0x18, 0x00] ++ (if pqRatchetMsg.isEmpty then [] else pbBytesField 5 pqRatchetMsg)

def dhOptNonZeroL266–271 ↗#

Check that an optional 32-byte X25519 shared secret (dh4?) is non-zero when present (PrivateKey::calculate_agreement in rust/core/src/curve.rs).

def dhOptNonZero (dh? : Option Bytes) : Bool := match dh? with | none => true | some dh => dh != List.replicate 32 0

def Model.initiateKeysL273–308 ↗#

Core PQXDH handshake initiation (<Pqxdh as Handshake>::initiate / pqxdh_initiate, pqxdh.rs:97-205, 194-237): verifies bundle signatures against the single wire key bundle.ikB, encapsulates against pqspkB, computes the 3 or 4 X25519 legs, and derives the 96-byte DRKey.

def Model.initiateKeys (P : Primitives) (inp : InitiateKeysInput) : Option (DRKey × HandshakeHdr) := do guard inp.trustedPeer -- 1. Verify XEdDSA signature on `SPK_B.serialize()` (`0x05 ‖ spkB`) under wire key `bundle.ikB` guard (P.sigVerify inp.bundle.ikB (encodeEC inp.bundle.spkB) inp.bundle.spkSig) -- 2. Verify XEdDSA signature on `PQSPK_B.serialize()` (`0x08 ‖ pqspkB`) under wire key `bundle.ikB` guard (P.sigVerify inp.bundle.ikB (encodeKEM inp.bundle.pqspkB) inp.bundle.pqspkSig) -- 3. Encapsulate against `PQSPK_B` (`pqxdh.rs:226-231`) let (ss, kemCt) ← P.kemEncaps inp.bundle.pqspkB inp.kemCoins -- 4. Ephemeral public key and 3 or 4 X25519 DH legs (`pqxdh.rs:198-224`); -- each `PrivateKey::calculate_agreement` (`rust/core/src/curve.rs`) rejects all-zero shared secrets. let ekAPk := P.x25519Base inp.ekASk let dh1 := P.x25519 inp.ikASk inp.bundle.spkB guard (dh1 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh2 := P.x25519 inp.ekASk inp.bundle.ikB guard (dh2 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh3 := P.x25519 inp.ekASk inp.bundle.spkB guard (dh3 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh4? := inp.bundle.opkB?.map (fun (_, opkPk) => P.x25519 inp.ekASk opkPk) guard (dhOptNonZero dh4?) -- 5. Derive 96-byte `DRKey = (rootKey, chainKey, pqrKey)` (`pqxdh.rs:233-236`) let secrets := buildSecrets dh1 dh2 dh3 dh4? ss let drKey := P.hkdfDerive96 secrets let hdr : HandshakeHdr := { ikAPk := inp.ikAPk ekAPk := ekAPk spkId := inp.bundle.spkId opkId? := inp.bundle.opkB?.map Prod.fst pqspkId := inp.bundle.pqspkId kemCt := kemCt } some (drKey, hdr)

def Model.acceptKeysL310–341 ↗#

Core PQXDH handshake acceptance (<Pqxdh as Handshake>::accept / pqxdh_accept, pqxdh.rs:208-291, 326-376, with mark_kyber_pre_key_used at pqxdh.rs:246-254 and storage/inmem.rs:247-265): checks is_canonical(ekAPk), computes 3 or 4 DH legs, decapsulates kemCt, and derives DRKey.

def Model.acceptKeys (P : Primitives) (inp : AcceptKeysInput) : Option DRKey := do guard inp.trustedPeer guard inp.replayOk -- 0. Wire EC public key 32-byte length checks (`curve.rs:95-115`) guard (inp.hdr.ikAPk.length == 32) guard (inp.hdr.ekAPk.length == 32) -- 1. Check `their_ephemeral_key.is_canonical()` first (`pqxdh.rs:328-333`) guard (P.isCanonical inp.hdr.ekAPk) -- 2. Compute 3 or 4 X25519 DH legs (`pqxdh.rs:339-366`); -- each `PrivateKey::calculate_agreement` (`rust/core/src/curve.rs`) rejects all-zero shared secrets. let dh1 := P.x25519 inp.spkBSk inp.hdr.ikAPk guard (dh1 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh2 := P.x25519 inp.ikBSk inp.hdr.ekAPk guard (dh2 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh3 := P.x25519 inp.spkBSk inp.hdr.ekAPk guard (dh3 != List.replicate 32 0) let dh4? ← match inp.hdr.opkId?, inp.opkBSk? with | none, none => some none | some _, some opkSk => some (some (P.x25519 opkSk inp.hdr.ekAPk)) | _, _ => none guard (dhOptNonZero dh4?) -- 3. Check `Ciphertext` wire length (`rust/protocol/src/kem.rs`, which rejects any slice whose -- length differs from `kyberCtLen`) and decapsulate under `PQSPK_B.sk` (`pqxdh.rs:368-373`) guard (inp.hdr.kemCt.length == kyberCtLen) let ss ← P.kemDecaps inp.pqspkBSk inp.hdr.kemCt -- 4. Assemble `[0xFFu8; 32]` (`pqxdh.rs:337`) + DH legs + `ss` and derive 96-byte `DRKey` (`pqxdh.rs:374-376`) let secrets := buildSecrets dh1 dh2 dh3 dh4? ss some (P.hkdfDerive96 secrets)

def Model.initiateL343–371 ↗#

Faithful first-message initiation (5-step key schedule; session.rs:200-285, ratchet.rs:67-112, triple_ratchet.rs:86-135): runs Model.initiateKeys to obtain drKey = (rk0, ck0, pqr0), then executes rootCreateChain(rk0, DH(ephA, spkB)) → chainKdf → spqrInitSend → deriveMsgKeys → aeadEnc.

def Model.initiate (P : Primitives) (inp : InitiateInput) : Option (DRKey × Bytes × Bytes × PreKeyMsg) := do let (drKey, hdr) ← Model.initiateKeys P inp.toInitiateKeysInput -- 6. Epoch-1 Root KDF: `root_key.create_chain(SPK_B.pk, eph_A¹.sk)` (`ratchet.rs:77-81`, `curve.rs`) let ephAPk := P.x25519Base inp.ephASk let dhRatchet := P.x25519 inp.ephASk inp.bundle.spkB guard (dhRatchet != List.replicate 32 0) let (rk1, ck1_0) := P.rootCreateChain drKey.rootKey dhRatchet -- 7. Epoch-1 Chain KDF: `ChainKey::message_keys` & `next_chain_key` (`ratchet/keys.rs:165-182`) let mkSeed := P.chainKdfSeed ck1_0 let ck1_1 := P.chainKdfNext ck1_0 -- 8. SPQR initial state & first send (`ratchet.rs:83-89`, `triple_ratchet.rs:97`) let (_pqrStA, spqrSalt?, pqRatchetMsg) ← P.spqrInitSend drKey.pqrKey inp.spqrCoins -- 9. Derive 80B `MessageKeys` with `optional_salt = spqrSalt?` (`ratchet/keys.rs:100-118`) let deriveMessageKeys := P.deriveMsgKeys mkSeed spqrSalt? -- 10. Encrypt inner `SignalMessage` under `deriveMessageKeys` and `firstMsgAD` let ad := firstMsgAD inp.ikAPk inp.bundle.ikB ephAPk pqRatchetMsg let aeadCt := P.aeadEnc deriveMessageKeys ad inp.plaintext let msg : PreKeyMsg := { hdr := hdr ephAPk := ephAPk pqRatchetMsg := pqRatchetMsg aeadCt := aeadCt } some (drKey, rk1, ck1_1, msg)

def Model.acceptL373–396 ↗#

Faithful first-message acceptance (5-step key schedule; session.rs:39-198, ratchet.rs:118-172, triple_ratchet.rs:215-298, session_management.rs:207-285): runs Model.acceptKeys to obtain drKey = (rk0, ck0, pqr0), then executes rootCreateChain(rk0, DH(spkB, ephA)) → chainKdf → spqrInitRecv → deriveMsgKeys → aeadDec.

def Model.accept (P : Primitives) (inp : AcceptInput) : Option (DRKey × Bytes × Bytes × Bytes) := do guard (inp.keysInp.hdr == inp.msg.hdr) let drKey ← Model.acceptKeys P inp.keysInp guard (inp.msg.ephAPk.length == 32) -- 5. Epoch-1 Root KDF receiving half-step: `create_chain(eph_A¹.pk, SPK_B.sk)` (`double_ratchet.rs:285`, `curve.rs`) let dhRatchet := P.x25519 inp.keysInp.spkBSk inp.msg.ephAPk guard (dhRatchet != List.replicate 32 0) let (rk1, ck1_0) := P.rootCreateChain drKey.rootKey dhRatchet -- 6. Epoch-1 Chain KDF: `ChainKey::message_keys` & `next_chain_key` let mkSeed := P.chainKdfSeed ck1_0 let ck1_1 := P.chainKdfNext ck1_0 -- 7. SPQR initial state & first receive (`ratchet.rs:146-152`, `triple_ratchet.rs:241-251`) let (_pqrStB, spqrSalt?) ← P.spqrInitRecv drKey.pqrKey inp.msg.pqRatchetMsg -- 8. Derive 80B `MessageKeys` with `optional_salt = spqrSalt?` let deriveMessageKeys := P.deriveMsgKeys mkSeed spqrSalt? -- 9. Verify 8-byte MAC and decrypt inner `SignalMessage` let ad := firstMsgAD inp.msg.hdr.ikAPk inp.keysInp.ikBPk inp.msg.ephAPk inp.msg.pqRatchetMsg let pt ← P.aeadDec deriveMessageKeys ad inp.msg.aeadCt some (drKey, rk1, ck1_1, pt)

def xeddsaVerifyRefL398–419 ↗#

Functional reference specification of Signal's XEdDSA signature verification (curve25519::verify_signature_for_multipart_message, rust/core/src/curve/curve25519.rs:119-160). The range check is on sig[63] &&& 0x60 because the sign bit (bit 7) is extracted and cleared before (s[31] & 0xE0) == 0 is tested.

def xeddsaVerifyRef (P : Primitives) (pk m sig : Bytes) : Bool := if pk.length == 32 && sig.length == 64 && ((sig.getD 63 0 &&& 0x60) == 0) then let signBit : UInt8 := (sig.getD 63 0 &&& 0x80) >>> 7 match P.montToEd pk signBit with | none => false | some edPk => let capA := P.compress edPk let minusCapA := P.edNeg edPk let capR := sig.take 32 let sRaw := sig.drop 32 let sClamped := sRaw.take 31 ++ [sRaw.getD 31 0 &&& 0x7F] let h := P.scalarFromWide (P.sha512 (capR ++ capA ++ m)) let sScalar := P.scalarFromBytesModOrder sClamped let capRCheck := P.compress (P.doubleScalarMulBasepoint h minusCapA sScalar) capRCheck == capR else false

def scalarIsInRangeL421–430 ↗#

Constant-time little-endian range check scalar_is_in_range from rust/core/src/curve.rs:176-186: returns true iff bit 7 of byte 31 is 0 ((pk.getD 31 0 &&& 0x80) == 0) and the little-endian 255-bit integer pk is strictly less than 2^255 - 19, i.e., not pk[0] >= 0xED ∧ pk[1..31] == [0xFF; 30] ∧ (pk[31] & 0x7F) == 0x7F.

def scalarIsInRange (pk : Bytes) : Bool := ((pk.getD 31 0 &&& 0x80) == 0) && !(pk.getD 0 0 >= 0xED && (pk.drop 1).take 30 == List.replicate 30 0xFF && (pk.getD 31 0 &&& 0x7F) == 0x7F)

def isCanonicalRefL432–440 ↗#

Functional reference specification of <libsignal_core::curve::PublicKey>::is_canonical (rust/core/src/curve.rs:156-191).

def isCanonicalRef (P : Primitives) (pk : Bytes) : Bool := if pk.length == 32 && ((pk.getD 31 0 &&& 0x80) == 0) && scalarIsInRange pk then match P.montToEd pk 0 with | some edPt => P.isTorsionFree edPt | none => false else false

def clampScalar25519 (sk : Bytes) : Bytes := let s := fitBytesRef 32 sk (s.take 1).map (fun b => b &&& 0xF8) ++ (s.drop 1).take 30 ++ ((s.drop 31).take 1).map (fun b => (b &&& 0x7F) ||| 0x40)

def onCurveKeyL692–699 ↗#

pk is an X25519 input on which scalar multiplication is determined by the scalar's residue modulo ±ℓ: either a canonical key (isCanonicalRef: 32 bytes, high bit clear, u < p, montToEd succeeds and torsion-free, hence a curve point of order exactly ℓ) or a point whose pow8 projection agrees with that of an honest base-point output (so, by x25519_pow8_congr, X25519 on pk behaves like X25519 on a prime-subgroup curve point). Twist points are excluded: they satisfy neither disjunct.

def onCurveKey (P : Primitives) (pk : Bytes) : Prop := P.isCanonical pk = true ∨ ∃ e, e.length = 32 ∧ P.pow8 pk = P.pow8 (P.x25519Base e)

def isValidDhTripleRefL701–712 ↗#

Reference DDH predicate, gated on onCurveKey: (X, Y, Z) is a DH triple iff both X and Y satisfy onCurveKey P and some scalar a with X = x25519Base a has pow8 Z = pow8 (x25519 a Y), or the same holds with X and Y swapped. Requiring onCurveKey P X and onCurveKey P Y rejects quadratic-twist and small-order points in either key slot, so the DDH oracle in GapDH, GapDhWithSign and GapSigEufCma never answers cross-curve queries on 8k₀ mod ℓ' (on onCurveKey inputs, x25519_congr_of_base_eq makes x25519 a Y independent of the choice of scalar a with x25519Base a = X). Law isValidDhTriple_eq_ref pins P.isValidDhTriple to this predicate.

def isValidDhTripleRef (P : Primitives) (X Y Z : Bytes) : Prop := onCurveKey P X ∧ onCurveKey P Y ∧ ((∃ a, X = P.x25519Base a ∧ P.pow8 Z = P.pow8 (P.x25519 a Y)) ∨ (∃ b, Y = P.x25519Base b ∧ P.pow8 Z = P.pow8 (P.x25519 b X)))

Kyber-1024 structural well-formedness laws on P : Primitives without perfect decapsulation correctness (kem_corr, DEV-PQ21): encapsulation/decapsulation totality on well-sized inputs and output byte lengths.

SPQR initial-step well-formedness laws on P : Primitives: initiator totality, initiator/responder salt agreement, and received salt length bound.

The send side follows by `spqr_corr`. A hypothesis of `CryptoWellFormedPrimitivesδ`: it narrows the `P` covered; real `spqr` (0 / 32) and SPQR off (`none`) satisfy it. -/ spqrInitRecv_salt_len : ∀ pqrKey pqMsg stB salt, P.spqrInitRecv pqrKey pqMsg = some (stB, some salt) → salt.length ≤ 32

structure WellFormedDhL754–846 ↗#

RFC 7748 X25519, canonicality, cofactor-8 subgroup projection (pow8), and DDH-oracle consistency laws on P : Primitives.

Satisfiability requirement. Every law below is required to hold for real RFC 7748 X25519 on ALL 32-byte inputs, including twist points and small-order points (an adversary may supply any 32 bytes as a public key). A real-X25519 witness: let pow8 Q := [c]Q where c is the CRT idempotent with c ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), c ≡ 0 (mod 8) on the curve and c' ≡ 1 (mod ℓ'), c' ≡ 0 (mod 4) on the twist, all torsion points mapping to 0^32 (encoded as a 32-byte u-coordinate); let isValidDhTriple X Y Z hold iff isValidDhTripleRef X Y Z (law isValidDhTriple_eq_ref). canon_x25519 and ddh_consistent_left carry hypotheses (canonical input, onCurveKey) because their unrestricted forms do not hold for this witness (and for real X25519 under any choice of pow8/isValidDhTriple).

structure WellFormedDh (P : Primitives) : Prop where x25519_clamp : ∀ sk pk, P.x25519 (clampScalar25519 sk) pk = P.x25519 sk pk x25519Base_clamp : ∀ sk, P.x25519Base (clampScalar25519 sk) = P.x25519Base sk /-- Clamped X25519 scalars are non-zero mod ℓ (`2^252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493`), and `x25519Base b` lies in the prime-order subgroup of Curve25519 (order ℓ), so scalar multiplication by a clamped scalar `a` never yields the identity / order-2 point `u = 0` (all-zero 32-byte shared secret in `rust/core/src/curve.rs` `PrivateKey::calculate_agreement`). -/ x25519_base_ne_zero : ∀ a b, a.length = 32 → b.length = 32 → P.x25519 a (P.x25519Base b) ≠ List.replicate 32 0 /-- On Curve25519, every clamped 32-byte scalar `s = clampScalar25519 a` is a multiple of 8 (`s = 8 * k` with `2^251 ≤ s < 2^255 < 8 * ℓ`, so `gcd(k, ℓ) = 1`), which annihilates the cofactor-8 torsion subgroup (`ℤ/8ℤ` on the curve, `ℤ/4ℤ` on the twist) and is invertible on the prime-order-`ℓ` subgroup; hence `[s] pk` produces the all-zero `u = 0` output iff `[8] pk` is the identity, independently of the clamped scalar `a`. -/ x25519_zero_iff : ∀ a1 a2 pk, a1.length = 32 → a2.length = 32 → pk.length = 32 → (P.x25519 a1 pk = List.replicate 32 0 ↔ P.x25519 a2 pk = List.replicate 32 0) x25519_comm : ∀ a b, P.x25519 a (P.x25519Base b) = P.x25519 b (P.x25519Base a) canon_base : ∀ e, P.isCanonical (P.x25519Base e) = true /-- Scalar multiplication preserves canonicity of canonical inputs. The unconditional form `∀ a pk, P.isCanonical (P.x25519 a pk) = true` fails for real X25519: `pk = 0^32` (and any small-order point) gives output `0^32`, which is not torsion-free, and twist points give twist outputs, which fail `montToEd`/`isTorsionFree`. Holds for real X25519: a canonical `pk` has order exactly `ℓ`; the clamped scalar is `s = 8k` with `0 < k < 2^252 < ℓ`, so `[s]pk` has order `ℓ` and is again canonical. -/ canon_x25519 : ∀ a pk, a.length = 32 → P.isCanonical pk = true → P.isCanonical (P.x25519 a pk) = true pow8_idemp : ∀ p, P.pow8 (P.pow8 p) = P.pow8 p pow8_x25519_comm : ∀ a b, P.pow8 (P.x25519 a (P.x25519Base b)) = P.pow8 (P.x25519 b (P.x25519Base a)) ddh_consistent : ∀ a b z, P.isValidDhTriple (P.x25519Base a) (P.x25519Base b) z = true ↔ P.pow8 z = P.pow8 (P.x25519 a (P.x25519Base b)) /-- Restricted to `onCurveKey P pk`. The unrestricted form over ALL `pk` contradicts `x25519_pow8_congr` at real X25519: take clamped `s1 = 2^254`, `s2 = 2^254 + 8δ` with `δ = ℓ - 2^252`, so `s1 + s2 = 8ℓ`. Then `x25519Base s1 = x25519Base s2` (since `s2 ≡ -s1 (mod ℓ)`), so the left-hand side `isValidDhTriple (x25519Base s1) pk z` is the same for both scalars, while on the twist point `u = 2` (order divisible by the large twist prime `ℓ'`) `x25519 s1 pk ≠ x25519 s2 pk` and `pow8` separates them, so the right-hand sides differ. On `onCurveKey` inputs both scalars agree (`x25519_congr_of_base_eq`), and the law holds for the witness in the structure docstring. -/ ddh_consistent_left : ∀ a pk z, onCurveKey P pk → (P.isValidDhTriple (P.x25519Base a) pk z = true ↔ P.pow8 z = P.pow8 (P.x25519 a pk)) ddh_symm : ∀ pk1 pk2 z, P.isValidDhTriple pk1 pk2 z = P.isValidDhTriple pk2 pk1 z /-- The DDH oracle is the reference predicate `isValidDhTripleRef` on every input (including rejecting non-`onCurveKey` inputs such as twist and small-order points). Without this law the oracle is constrained only on `(base, base)` and `(base, onCurveKey)` inputs and by symmetry, so a `P` whose oracle answers `(x25519Base a, Y, Z)` for twist points `Y` with bits of `8k₀ mod ℓ'` would satisfy the other laws and make `GapDH` / `GapDhWithSign` easy. `ddh_symm` follows from this law, and `ddh_consistent` from it and `x25519_comm`. -/ isValidDhTriple_eq_ref : ∀ X Y Z, P.isValidDhTriple X Y Z = true ↔ isValidDhTripleRef P X Y Z /-- Restricted to 32-byte public keys. The unrestricted form fails for `pqxdhModelPrims`: `x25519 a pk` fits `pk` to 32 bytes (`u8Vec 32`), so a 33-byte `p' = x25519Base 0 ++ [0]` has `x25519 a p' = x25519 a (x25519Base 0) ≠ x25519 a 0^32`, preventing `pow8 p'` from mapping either to `pow8 0^32` (by `x25519_pow8_congr` + `x25519_inj_pow8`) or to `pow8 (x25519Base 0)` (by `pow8_base_len`). For 32-byte `pk1, pk2`, equal `pow8` projections mean `pk1` and `pk2` differ only by cofactor torsion, which clamping (`8k`) annihilates. -/ x25519_pow8_congr : ∀ a pk1 pk2, pk1.length = 32 → pk2.length = 32 → P.pow8 pk1 = P.pow8 pk2 → P.x25519 a pk1 = P.x25519 a pk2 /-- (True for real X25519.) Scalars with equal base-point outputs agree on every `onCurveKey` input. Equal `x25519Base` outputs give `s1 ≡ ±s2 (mod ℓ)`. For a canonical `pk` (order `ℓ`), `u([s]Q) = u([-s]Q)`, so the outputs agree. For the torsion disjunct `pow8 pk = pow8 (x25519Base e)`, `x25519_pow8_congr` reduces both sides to `x25519 sᵢ (x25519Base e) = x25519 e (x25519Base sᵢ)`, which agree. The `onCurveKey` hypothesis is necessary: on the twist point `u = 2` the pair `s1 = 2^254`, `s2 = 2^254 + 8(ℓ - 2^252)` has equal base outputs but different outputs (the twist subgroup has order `ℓ' ≠ ℓ`). -/ x25519_congr_of_base_eq : ∀ a1 a2 pk, a1.length = 32 → a2.length = 32 → onCurveKey P pk → P.x25519Base a1 = P.x25519Base a2 → P.x25519 a1 pk = P.x25519 a2 pk canon_pow8_inj : ∀ pk1 pk2, P.isCanonical pk1 = true → P.isCanonical pk2 = true → P.pow8 pk1 = P.pow8 pk2 → pk1 = pk2 x25519_len : ∀ k p, (P.x25519 k p).length = 32 x25519Base_len : ∀ k, (P.x25519Base k).length = 32 pow8_len : ∀ p, (P.pow8 p).length = 32 isCanonical_eq_isCanonicalRef : ∀ pk, P.isCanonical pk = isCanonicalRef P pk

structure WellFormedSigL848–864 ↗#

XEdDSA signing/verification, single-key public-key identity (sigPkGen = x25519Base), SHA-512 reference link, and Curve25519 scalar and Edwards-point byte lengths on P : Primitives.

structure WellFormedSig (P : Primitives) : Prop where sha512Compress_len : ∀ st blk, (P.sha512Compress st blk).length = 64 sha512_eq_ref : ∀ m, P.sha512 m = sha512Ref P m sha512_len : ∀ m, (P.sha512 m).length = 64 sigPkGen_eq_x25519Base : P.sigPkGen = P.x25519Base scalarMul_len : ∀ a b, (P.scalarMul a b).length = 32 scalarAdd_len : ∀ a b, (P.scalarAdd a b).length = 32 scalarFromBytesModOrder_len : ∀ b, (P.scalarFromBytesModOrder b).length = 32 scalarFromWide_len : ∀ b, (P.scalarFromWide b).length = 32 montToEd_len : ∀ u s pt, P.montToEd u s = some pt → pt.length = 160 edNeg_len : ∀ pt, (P.edNeg pt).length = 160 doubleScalarMulBasepoint_len : ∀ h a s, (P.doubleScalarMulBasepoint h a s).length = 160 compress_len : ∀ pt, (P.compress pt).length = 32 sigVerify_eq_xeddsaVerifyRef : ∀ pk m sig, P.sigVerify pk m sig = xeddsaVerifyRef P pk m sig sig_corr : ∀ sk msg r, P.sigVerify (P.sigPkGen sk) msg (P.sigSign sk msg r) = true

structure WellFormedKdfL866–874 ↗#

SHA-256 compression block length and reference-construction equations for the handshake, Epoch-1 root, chain, and message-key HKDF/HMAC derivations on P : Primitives.

structure WellFormedKdf (P : Primitives) : Prop where sha256Compress_len : ∀ st blk, (P.sha256Compress st blk).length = 32 hkdfDerive96_eq_ref : ∀ secrets, P.hkdfDerive96 secrets = hkdfDerive96Ref P secrets rootCreateChain_eq_ref : ∀ rk dh, P.rootCreateChain rk dh = rootCreateChainRef P rk dh chainKdfSeed_eq_ref : ∀ ck, P.chainKdfSeed ck = chainKdfSeedRef P ck chainKdfNext_eq_ref : ∀ ck, P.chainKdfNext ck = chainKdfNextRef P ck deriveMsgKeys_eq_ref : ∀ mkSeed salt?, P.deriveMsgKeys mkSeed salt? = deriveMsgKeysRef P mkSeed salt?

structure WellFormedAeadL876–885 ↗#

AES-256 block-cipher lengths/roundtrip and first-message CBC-HMAC AEAD reference links and decryption roundtrip on P : Primitives.

structure WellFormedAead (P : Primitives) : Prop where aesEncBlock_len : ∀ k blk, (P.aesEncBlock k blk).length = 16 aesDecBlock_len : ∀ k blk, (P.aesDecBlock k blk).length = 16 aesBlock_corr : ∀ k blk, k.length = 32 → blk.length = 16 → P.aesDecBlock k (P.aesEncBlock k blk) = blk aeadEnc_eq_ref : ∀ mk ad pt, P.aeadEnc mk ad pt = aes256CbcHmacEncRef P mk ad pt aeadDec_eq_ref : ∀ mk ad ct, P.aeadDec mk ad ct = aes256CbcHmacDecRef P mk ad ct aead_corr : ∀ mk ad pt, P.aeadDec mk ad (P.aeadEnc mk ad pt) = some pt

structure WellFormedPrimitivesδL887–896 ↗#

Structural and algebraic well-formedness of P : Primitives without the perfect KEM decapsulation correctness law kem_corr (DEV-PQ21), assembled from the six component bundles WellFormedKemδ, WellFormedSpqr, WellFormedDh, WellFormedSig, WellFormedKdf, and WellFormedAead. KEM correctness is assumed separately via KemDeltaCorrect P δ (Computational/Specifications/Assumptions/KemCorrect.lean), while proof-side WellFormedPrimitives (LibsignalBinary/Proofs/SpecLemmas/SignalPqxdh/ModelProofDefs.lean) extends WellFormedPrimitivesδ with kem_corr.

structure WellFormedPrimitivesδ (P : Primitives) : Prop extends WellFormedKemδ P, WellFormedSpqr P, WellFormedDh P, WellFormedSig P, WellFormedKdf P, WellFormedAead P

def PqxdhCorrectL898–928 ↗#

Functional correctness of PQXDH: for every honest run (authentic bundle and signatures, trusted peers, no replay, KEM and SPQR succeed), Model.initiateKeys/Model.acceptKeys and Model.initiate/Model.accept all succeed with identical (drKey, rk1, ck1_1) and Bob recovers Alice's plaintext. The correctness conjunct of the PQXDH headline statement (Computational/Specifications/Pqxdh/Security/Headline.lean).

def PqxdhCorrect (P : Primitives) : Prop := ∀ (initInp : InitiateInput) (accKeysInp : AcceptKeysInput) (ss kemCt : Bytes), initInp.trustedPeer = true → accKeysInp.trustedPeer = true → accKeysInp.replayOk = true → P.sigVerify initInp.bundle.ikB (encodeEC initInp.bundle.spkB) initInp.bundle.spkSig = true → P.sigVerify initInp.bundle.ikB (encodeKEM initInp.bundle.pqspkB) initInp.bundle.pqspkSig = true → initInp.ikAPk = P.x25519Base initInp.ikASk → (initInp.bundle.ikB = P.x25519Base accKeysInp.ikBSk ∧ accKeysInp.ikBPk = initInp.bundle.ikB) → (initInp.bundle.spkB = P.x25519Base accKeysInp.spkBSk ∧ accKeysInp.spkBPk = initInp.bundle.spkB) → (initInp.bundle.opkB?.map Prod.snd = accKeysInp.opkBSk?.map P.x25519Base ∧ initInp.bundle.opkB?.isSome = accKeysInp.opkBSk?.isSome) → P.kemEncaps initInp.bundle.pqspkB initInp.kemCoins = some (ss, kemCt) → P.kemDecaps accKeysInp.pqspkBSk kemCt = some ss → (P.spqrInitSend (P.hkdfDerive96 (buildSecrets (P.x25519 initInp.ikASk initInp.bundle.spkB) (P.x25519 initInp.ekASk initInp.bundle.ikB) (P.x25519 initInp.ekASk initInp.bundle.spkB) (initInp.bundle.opkB?.map (fun (_, opkPk) => P.x25519 initInp.ekASk opkPk)) ss)).pqrKey initInp.spqrCoins).isSome = true → ∃ drKey hdr rk1 ck1_1 msg, Model.initiateKeys P initInp.toInitiateKeysInput = some (drKey, hdr) ∧ Model.acceptKeys P { accKeysInp with hdr := hdr } = some drKey ∧ Model.initiate P initInp = some (drKey, rk1, ck1_1, msg) ∧ Model.accept P { keysInp := { accKeysInp with hdr := hdr }, msg := msg } = some (drKey, rk1, ck1_1, initInp.plaintext)
end SignalPqxdh
